### 1. What the user expresses; simulator role

- Target: "you appealed the decision that denied your unemployment benefits and ... need your appeal hearing to be held by video hearing". Mode: video, "the whole reason you are calling". Authorisation: she pre-agrees "If the agent explains that something has to be done on the Department's side before the video session can be booked, tell them that is fine and they can go ahead", and will run the booking herself with "exactly the appeal docket number and the number of days the agent gives you".
- She does not know the docket number ("ask the agent to look it up"). Conditional facts (mailed October 2; ASL interpreter asked in writing; no hearing notice received; laptop with camera; audiologist letter and written statement already mailed) are passive if/else answers only. She executes the user tool only when handed over. Nothing in the script pushes the procedure.
- Identity: phone 6085553417, SSN last4 3582, ZIP 53748 (+ DOB, email). `verify_caller_identity` with phone+last4+ZIP -> "Identity verified ... (3 detail(s) matched on this attempt)".

### 2. Act / wait / refuse at the frozen moment

Act now. Grounds:
- Video is available on this docket: video_hearing_session_booking: "a party may ask ... for a video hearing on any docket that holds hearings"; hearing_calendar_terms: Separation Issue "Hearing held | yes".
- The booking is not a postponement: "A change of hearing mode booked as a video session is not a postponement: it needs no postponement request or decision, is not subject to the postponement lead time, does not count toward the party's postponements and is not held to the reschedule window". So no lead-time/max-postponement test bars it.
- But the appeal record shows `'status': 'filed'`, `'hearing_date': ''`. video_hearing_session_booking: "On an appeal at filed status, a video session is booked only after the appeal stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on record." Hence the video session cannot be booked first; the first hearing must be set (Department side) now, which is permitted: hearing_setting_and_notice (b) "A hearing is set only while the appeal status is filed, scheduled or dismissed" (filed -> yes); first_hearing_docketing "An appeal standing at filed status on a docket that holds hearings is due to be docketed and set for its first hearing."
- Nothing makes the agent wait: the appeal is timely (determination mailed 2026-09-25, filed 2026-10-02 by mail, Separation Issue deadline 21 days -> 2026-10-16), `late_filing_reason: 'none'`.

### 4. Scored parameters

Two numbers are produced by the agent: the first-setting notice period (docketing tool) and the video session notice period (handed to the user).

**4a. First-setting notice period (first_hearing_date_computation + factors)**

Baseline text: "The first hearing date is the date that falls the first-setting target's number of calendar days after the day the first-setting clock starts. The first-setting clock starts on the appeal's filing date. The first-setting target is the docket's scheduling target days. When the first hearing date found this way is fewer than the docket's notice minimum days after today, ... notice minimum days after today instead. A first hearing date that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday moves to the following Monday."

Tier rules found from the records:
- Clock start (first_setting_clock_start): record words `filing_channel: 'mail'`, `late_filing_reason: 'none'` -> "none | mail | the presumed receipt date: 3 calendar days after the postmark date" -> 2026-10-02 + 3 = **2026-10-05**.
- Target (claimant_hearing_target): appellant_role claimant; appealed claim's payment history shows no benefit payment issued; window "dates later than the same day of the month two months before today" = after 2026-08-14 through 2026-10-14; certifications in window: 08-17, 08-24, 08-31, 09-08, 09-14, 09-21, 09-28, 10-05, 10-12 = 9 (08-10 excluded) >= 3 -> "claimant | none | 3 or more | 14 days" -> **14**.
- Federal records lead (federal_program_records_lead): claim variant UCFE -> **10** ("Unemployment Compensation for Federal Employees (UCFE) | 10 calendar days").
- Interpreter lead (interpreter_lead_first_hearing): latest (only) interpreter request american_sign_language -> **10**.
- Subpoena lead (subpoena_lead_first_hearing): one subpoena request with status received -> "exactly one | 7 calendar days" -> **7**.
- Each lead doc: "moved later by this lead before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied".

Date found = 2026-10-05 + 14 + 10 + 10 + 7 = 2026-10-05 + 41 = Sunday 2026-11-15. Notice minimum (hearing_calendar_terms: Separation Issue 7) -> 2026-10-21; 11-15 is later, stands. Weekend: Sunday -> Monday **2026-11-16**. Notice period from today 2026-10-14 (day 0) = **33**.

Tool check: docket call with 33 returned `'status': 'scheduled', 'hearing_date': '2026-11-16', 'hearing_mode': 'telephone'`.

Fall-back (baseline only): filing date 2026-10-02 + 30 = Sunday 2026-11-01 -> Monday 2026-11-02 -> **19** (definite, differs from 33).

**4b. Video session notice period (video_session_date_computation + factors)**

Baseline text: "The video session date is the set hearing date moved later by the video block gap. The video block gap is the standard video block days, 5 calendar days. A video session date that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday moves to the following Monday."

Input: set hearing date after docketing = 2026-11-16 (from the docket receipt / find_appeals `'hearing_date': '2026-11-16'`).

Tier rules found from the records:
- Video block gap (video_block_gap_interpreted_hearings): latest interpreter request ASL ("a language other than Spanish (American Sign Language included)"), Separation Issue hearing length 60 -> "10 days".
- Accommodation review (video_accommodation_review): medical_statement exhibit received + latest request ASL -> **5**.
- Exhibit preparation (video_exhibit_preparation): claimant appellant submitted 2 exhibits -> "two or more | 5" -> **5**.
- Identity check (video_identity_check): IDV case on the appealed claim verified through "In-Person Proofing — American Job Center" -> "verified, through a pathway other than a Video Trusted Referee Session | 3" -> **3**.
- Each add-on doc: "These days are added to the video block gap, and the set hearing date is moved later by the total before the calendar-day rule is applied."
- Calendar-day rule (video_session_weekday_assignment): "On the Separation Issue and the Able and Available Issue dockets a video session date moves to the first Tuesday or Thursday on or after the date found".

Total gap 10+5+5+3 = 23. 2026-11-16 + 23 = Wednesday 2026-12-09 -> Separation Issue: Wednesday +1 -> Thursday **2026-12-10**. Notice period from 2026-10-14 = **57**.

Tool check: user booking with 57 returned `'hearing_date': '2026-12-10', 'hearing_time': '13:00', 'hearing_mode': 'video'`.

Fall-back (video baseline only, on the correct set date): 2026-11-16 + 5 = Saturday 11-21 -> Monday 11-23 -> **40** (definite, differs). Fully naive chain (both baselines): 2026-11-02 + 5 = Saturday 11-07 -> Monday 11-09 -> 26.

Findability (words of the records -> document):

- subpoena request `request_status: received` -> "Subpoena Desk Note — First Hearing Lead for Pending Subpoena Requests".

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Problems: P1 = video session booking (customer's own write, root); P2 = docketing / first hearing setting (agent write).

- Hop P1 -> P2 (**state-derived**). Visible sentence on the blocked side (video_hearing_session_booking, "Status of the appeal"): "On an appeal at filed status, a video session is booked only after the appeal stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on record." Query: `find_appeals` -> `'status': 'filed'`, `'hearing_date': ''` — the state does not hold. Search with the sentence's words "scheduled status" / "first hearing setting" -> first_hearing_docketing: "Docketing moves the appeal from filed to scheduled status: the appeal is docketed and its first hearing is set" and "the first hearing setting is entered on the appeal's activity as a hearing-setting record ... marked as the first (initial) setting". That document names its own tool `docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da` (agent-side). The video document does not name the docketing tool or the docketing document. Also the video computation's own input ("the hearing date currently set on the appeal record") is empty until P2 is done, which independently confirms the order.
- P2 has no visible prerequisite sentence; its status condition (filed) holds.
- Order: P2 (agent) then P1 (user). Tree derived: yes, no hop pre-solved.

### Two-way counter-proof

- "Do only the one thing asked" (hand over the video booking now): excluded by the visible sentence above plus record `status: filed`; and the video computation would have no set hearing date as input. (Note: the runtime booking tool itself accepted a call on the filed appeal in a scratch session — it does not guard the status; the exclusion is by the visible rule, not by a tool error.)
- Closest alternative clock start (filing date 2026-10-02): excluded by first_setting_clock_start "none | mail | presumed receipt date: 3 calendar days after the postmark date".
- Alternative target 30 (docket target): excluded by claimant_hearing_target (no benefit payment in window; 9 >= 3 certified weeks). Alternative 18 excluded (9 is not fewer than 3).
- Lead alternatives: UCX 7 excluded (claim is UCFE); interpreter contract lead 7 excluded (ASL); subpoena 10 excluded (only one received).
- Video gap 5/7 excluded (ASL is "other than Spanish", 60 min >= 60). Accommodation 3 excluded (latest is ASL). Prep 3 excluded (2 exhibits). Identity 0/6 excluded (verified, not via Video Trusted Referee Session).
- Weekend-only rule (would give Wed 12-09 standing, 56) excluded by video_session_weekday_assignment for Separation Issue (Tuesday/Thursday).
- Postponement framing (3-business-day lead, 1 postponement, 14-day reset) excluded by "A change of hearing mode booked as a video session is not a postponement".
- In-person alternative excluded by the user ("say no, you want video").
